meta.title: PWM LED 'breathing' fade with gamma correction
meta.tools: C firmware on a simulated MCU (eelab HAL), Python logic-analyser decoding, Wokwi sketch
meta.summary: Fade an LED in and out with 8-bit software PWM at 1 kHz, using a gamma-2.2 lookup table so the perceived brightness ramps linearly; decode the pin log to verify PWM frequency, duty resolution and the breathing period.
meta.problem: A linear duty-cycle ramp looks wrong to the eye — the LED seems to jump to full brightness. Why, and how does gamma correction fix it?
meta.theory:
Perceived brightness ∝ luminance^(1/2.2) (approximately), so duty = (step/255)^{2.2} makes perceived brightness linear in the step.
PWM period = 256 ticks × tick; with a 3.9 µs tick → 1 kHz (well above flicker fusion). A 2-s breathing cycle = 512 steps × ≈3.9 ms.
meta.method:
Firmware: timer-driven 8-bit PWM (counter compare), gamma LUT computed at start-up (integer), brightness index triangle 0→255→0 over 2 s. The
simulation runs 4 s; Python measures every period and high time from the GPIO log.

metrics.quantity: Without gamma: perceived brightness at 25 % of the ramp
